title: Glossary
description: A per-language terminology file. Maps source-language terms to their approved translations for a given locale. Used by the validator to enforce consistency: when a keyTerm in a translated lesson includes a sourceTerm, the validator checks that the translation matches this glossary.

language.description: BCP-47 tag of the target language for this glossary. This is the language of the 'translation' field in each term. Example: 'it', 'de', 'es-419'.

sourceLanguage.description: BCP-47 tag of the language used in the 'sourceTerm' field of each entry. Must match the source language of your content files. Example: 'en'.

version.description: Glossary version. Increment when terms are added, removed, or changed. Content files can reference this version to signal their glossary compliance level.

maintainer.description: Name or role of the person responsible for maintaining this glossary.

terms.description: The term list. Each entry maps one source term to its approved translation. Terms must be unique by sourceTerm within a glossary.

sourceTerm.description: The term in the source language (sourceLanguage). This is the lookup key — it must match the sourceTerm field in translated lesson keyTerms entries.

translation.description: The approved translation in the target language (language). Do not use this field for literal translations — record the term that is actually used in context in this language.

definition.description: Optional definition of the source term, in the source language. Helps translators understand the term's scope when no reference is available.

notes.description: Any notes for the translator or reviewer: usage constraints, gender agreement, false friends to avoid, regional variants.

domain.description: The subject domain this term belongs to. Useful when the same source term has different translations in different domains (e.g. 'curriculum' in education vs. CV context).

forbidden.description: Alternative translations that MUST NOT be used for this term in this language. Document any near-miss terms that have been rejected in review.

updatedAt.description: When this specific term entry was last updated. Useful for auditing freshness.

terms.definition: The top number in a fraction — how many parts are taken.
terms.notes: Gender: masculine (il numeratore). No regional variants within Italy.

terms.definition: The bottom number in a fraction — the total number of parts.
A document summarising a job applicant's education, experience, and skills.
terms.notes: Keep in Latin form — 'curriculum vitae' is the established term in Italian professional contexts. Abbreviation 'CV' is also widely accepted. Do not translate as 'résumé'.

terms.definition: A document accompanying the CV, introducing the applicant.
terms.notes: Some job postings use 'lettera motivazionale' — both are acceptable. Prefer 'lettera di presentazione' for consistency unless the posting specifies otherwise.
